title: fix(guest-supervisor): a verified-local agent job can run the pinned Node toolchain: node/npm first on its PATH, with untracked node_modules kept out of the candidate export (prerequisite of task-7d154d34)
description:
Carved out of task-7d154d34 (architect-3669a6f6, 2026-11-06) so the code lands before that row records the governor's re-certify. task-7d154d34 dependsOn this row and keeps the docs, the CERTIFICATION.md table, the re-certify of both hosts and the DoD 8 re-run.

(1) OBJECTIVE. In a verified-local seat VM, a worker or QA agent job can run the project's Node toolchain in place. The governor's DoD 8 Windows real-VM run (task-1a8f1d0e, 2026-11-06) found the agent reporting "no node or npm in this workspace" (exit 127). Cause, in scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py:
- JOB_PATH = '/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin' (:910) is the agent job's whole PATH (start_job :986, env at :1017).
- agent-seat.mjs installs the pinned toolchain at seat-start into TOOLCHAIN '/opt/moe/toolchain' (:911), and only check_job puts its bin first: `'PATH': toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH` (:1434).
The same fix must keep what an in-place `npm ci` writes out of the candidate. Export (class :793, export() :867) walks the whole workspace with no ignore rule, so node_modules would be exported: thousands of entries, and the node_modules/.bin symlinks that the host import refuses (SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED, or SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED past 10,000 entries). And any exported byte refuses a QA job (SEAT_JOB_QA_CANDIDATE_REFUSED, agent-seat.mjs:273: a QA candidate must be empty).

(2) DELIVERABLE.
- start_job gains `toolchain=TOOLCHAIN` (injectable from Python only, like check_job's) and sets the agent job env PATH to `toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH`, the check job's exact form. Worker and QA jobs both go through start_job, so this one change covers both roles.
- Export skips a directory named exactly `node_modules` (a real directory by lstat, never a symlink) when no manifest path lies under it. Such a directory is neither walked nor emitted, so it adds no entry, delete, byte or visit past its own name.
  - A node_modules directory that holds a manifest path is walked exactly as today.
  - A node_modules symlink still exports as 'symlink', and a regular file named node_modules as 'file'.
- The supervisor's comments say both: the bridge job's PATH, and the export mode's skip.
- CERTIFICATION_PINS.supervisorSha256 (packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/certificationEvidence.ts:28, today 616463b7…) moves to the new file's sha256 in the same diff (mem:decision-certification-evidence-pins), so readiness accepts only reports of the new supervisor.
- After this lands, every host's stored certification report stops matching. Verified-local readiness then stays not-ready on Windows and WSL until the governor re-certifies (task-7d154d34). That is expected.

(3) NOT IN SCOPE.
- The role docs, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the docs/CERTIFICATION.md table, the re-certify runs and the DoD 8 re-run: all task-7d154d34's.
- check_job and every other supervisor mode.
- The toolchain install, any scripts/local-runner/*.mjs, the host import and admission, and the check VMs' offline installs.
- The agent job's network: still no netns, the guest's own network, unlike check jobs.
- No .gitignore handling or other directory names: only node_modules.

(4) VERIFICATION. Run one gate in a git-archive snapshot of the full tree (never npm in the shared checkout: global rail), under a Linux-only Node 24 PATH:
- `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs`;
- `npx vitest run src/delivery/certificationEvidence.test.ts` in the snapshot's packages/moe-daemon, after npm ci there.
The planner pins the exact checkRef inside the 20-minute gate budget.
definitionOfDone: scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs: J3 and J4 expect the agent job's PATH '/opt/moe/toolchain/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin' for the worker (claude) and QA (codex) jobs. A new J row injects a toolchain whose bin holds a stub `node` and a `#!/usr/bin/env node` `npm`, and proves a job's bare `node` and `npm` both resolve to that bin (npm through its env shebang), ahead of any node in /usr/local/bin.

scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs export rows: an untracked node_modules tree (files, a .bin symlink and a nested node_modules, at the workspace root and under a package directory) exports nothing. A manifest path under node_modules still exports its edit, its delete and a new sibling file. A node_modules symlink still exports as 'symlink', and a regular file named node_modules as 'file'.

CERTIFICATION_PINS.supervisorSha256 equals the sha256 of the new guest-supervisor.py, so the certificationEvidence.test.ts drift row is green. A new row refuses a report that carries the previous pin 616463b7d33cf5d0efa79d5540d0911a5c56a6899b63b244ce60116e1aec0c0e with CERTIFICATION_REPORT_SUPERVISOR.

The diff touches exactly scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py, the two local-runner test files, packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/certificationEvidence.ts and its test. In the supervisor, check_job and every mode other than the bridge job and export are byte-unchanged.
The snapshot gate (the four local-runner test files and certificationEvidence.test.ts) passes fresh, and its output is the complete_task evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1: a worker or QA agent job gets the pinned Node toolchain first on its PATH. Reference bytes, validated at planning: mem:task-task-ccbff5c686c44501a376539bc9e54804-prototype (re-wrap and finish its comments as noted there). Edit with this seat's own editor (Edit on Claude, apply_patch on a codex exec seat), never a shell write.

SUPERVISOR, scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py:
- start_job (:986): append the keyword `toolchain=TOOLCHAIN` after `peer_uid=peer_uid`. It is a Python-only seam like check_job's (:1401). main() (:1722) already forwards **seams to start_job and stays byte-unchanged.
- Its env (:1017): `'PATH': toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH`, check_job's exact form (:1434). Nothing else in env or spawn changes. In particular there is no netns key: the agent job keeps the guest's own network, and J3 pins spawn.
- Wrap that env dict so no added line exceeds 120 chars (move `'LANG': 'C.UTF-8',` to the next line).
- Comments, each changed or added line at most 120 chars:
  - start_job's comment block (:979-985) adds toolchain to its Python-only seams. It also says the job's PATH puts toolchain/bin first, as a check job's does. That bin holds the pinned Node, which agent-seat.mjs installs at seat start through the 'toolchain' mode.
  - The TOOLCHAIN comment (:911) says agent and check jobs both put its bin first.
  - Never rewrap header lines that describe other modes.

TESTS, scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:
- J3 (:1703) and J4 (:1761): the expected PATH becomes exactly '/opt/moe/toolchain/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'. task-7d154d34's gate greps this literal. J3 covers the worker (claude) and QA (codex) jobs; J4 covers the QA job's real environment.
- HELD (:1737) gains an optional second parameter `extra = ''`, appended to the main() keywords after `agent_socket=None`. J4's HELD('None') call stays unchanged.
- New row J5, named 'J5 ...': task-7d154d34 re-runs `^[JX][0-9]+ `. Place it after J4, with `{ skip: NO_GUEST, timeout: 30_000 }`; it reads no /proc, so macOS runs it too. In its own mkdtemp dir, removed in t.after:
  - toolchain/bin/node: a 0755 `#!/bin/sh` stub printing `toolchain node $*`.
  - toolchain/bin/npm: exactly `#!/usr/bin/env node` plus a newline, 0755.
  - shadow/node and shadow/npm: 0755 stubs printing `shadow node` and `shadow npm`.
- The J5 harness sets `m.JOB_PATH = <shadow> + ':' + m.JOB_PATH`, which start_job reads at call time. shadow then stands where a node in /usr/local/bin would; a non-root test cannot write /usr/local/bin. The harness passes `, toolchain=<toolchain>` through HELD's extra.
- The Python probe prints os.environ['PATH'], then shutil.which('node') and shutil.which('npm'), then the stdout of subprocess.run(['node', 'one']) and subprocess.run(['npm', 'two']), each with check=True.
- For JOB and for QA_JOB, the exit must be EXIT, and stdout must equal exactly `<tc>/bin:<shadow>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin\n<tc>/bin/node <tc>/bin/npm\ntoolchain node one\ntoolchain node <tc>/bin/npm two\n`. The last line proves that npm's env shebang found the toolchain's node through PATH.

Planning evidence: J3, J4 and J5 were green with the change and red on the base supervisor. The JOB_PATH-first mutant failed J3, J4 and J5. The mutant using TOOLCHAIN in place of the toolchain seam failed J5.

Error handling: start_job keeps every refusal (74, 65, 71, 66) in the same order. Only the value of the env's PATH changes, so this step adds no new error handling path.
implementationPlan.note: start_job gains toolchain=TOOLCHAIN and PATH = toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH (check_job's form); comments updated, no added line over 120 chars. J3/J4 expect the new PATH, HELD takes an optional extra, new J5 proves node/npm (npm via env shebang) resolve to the toolchain bin ahead of a shadow dir. J3-J5 pass (node --test, 3/3).

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 2: the export never carries an untracked node_modules directory. Reference bytes: mem:task-task-ccbff5c686c44501a376539bc9e54804-prototype. Use this seat's own editor.

SUPERVISOR, guest-supervisor.py, class Export (:793):
- __init__ (:798) builds `self.vendored` once: the node_modules directory paths that hold a manifest path. Split each manifest path on '/'; every prefix whose LAST segment is exactly 'node_modules' qualifies, never the path's own final segment. The prototype is a two-line set comprehension over `known`.
- directory() (:808): inside `if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):` (:823), before the os.open, add `if name == 'node_modules' and path not in self.vendored: continue`, with a short comment.
  - The listing loop has already counted that name in self.visited. Nothing under it is listed, opened, emitted, counted, or added to seen.
- Only that exact name is skipped: case-sensitive, never a prefix. It is skipped only when lstat says it is a real directory. A symlink or a regular file named node_modules falls through to today's 'symlink' and 'file' frames; the host's SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED stays the fail-closed path for a node_modules link.
- The rule is per directory. An untracked node_modules nested inside a tracked one is skipped too.
- Suppose the manifest held a file at the path node_modules itself, and that path is now a directory. The directory holds no manifest path, so it is skipped, and finish() still emits that path's delete.
- Comments: the Export docstring (:794-796) states the skip, and so does the header's export clause (:8-9). Change only that clause's own line or lines, wrapped at 120. Never change the lines that describe other modes.
- Add no module-level statement. checkRefs[1] lets only start_job and Export differ from the existing top-level statements at fb142d89.

TESTS, scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (the X rows from :5332):
- workspaceIn(t) (:5336) gains `base = EXPORT_BASE`. Existing calls are unchanged.
- New row 'X8 ...' after X3. In one workspaceIn(t), create a node_modules both at the root and under src (a tracked package directory). Each holds dep/index.js, a nested dep/node_modules/deep/x.js, and .bin/dep, a symlink to ../dep/index.js.
  - exportIn must give status 0 and exactly [{kind: 'end', entries: 0}].
  - The same workspace with `m.WALK_LIMIT = 8` must exit 0, and with 7 must exit 65: EXPORT_BASE's 6 names plus the 2 skipped names, never a name inside one.
- New row 'X9 ...', a table like X2's over workspaceIn(t, base).
  - With base = [...EXPORT_BASE, fileOf('lib/node_modules/kept/a.js', 'A'), fileOf('node_modules/kept/index.js', 'K')]:
    - an edit of node_modules/kept/index.js;
    - an edit of lib/node_modules/kept/a.js, under a package directory;
    - a delete of node_modules/kept/index.js;
    - a new sibling, node_modules/new.js.
    Each exports exactly its file and data frames, or its delete, then end(1).
    An untracked node_modules/kept/node_modules/x/i.js exports [end(0)].
  - With base = EXPORT_BASE:
    - a node_modules symlink to src exports [{kind: 'symlink', path: 'node_modules'}, end(1)];
    - a regular file named node_modules exports its file and data frames;
    - directories named 'Node_modules' and 'node_modules.old', each holding f, export both files, then end(2).

Planning evidence: X8 and X9 were green with the change; the base supervisor fails both. Each of these mutants failed X9:
- skip every node_modules;
- a prefix match;
- a case-folded match;
- a vendored set holding only top-level paths;
- the skip moved before the S_ISDIR test.

Error handling: export() keeps its exit codes (65, 71, 74) and its drop-before-walk order. The skip opens nothing, so it adds no failure path.
implementationPlan.note: Export gains self.vendored (node_modules dirs holding a manifest path) and skips a real directory named exactly node_modules not in it, before os.open; docstring and header export clause state it. workspaceIn takes a base; new X8 (untracked tree exports end(0), WALK_LIMIT 8 ok / 7 refused) and X9 (tracked node_modules walked, symlink/file/other names still export). - Does any added line contain a project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string?

Fix what you find, then re-run step 4's command fresh before moe.complete_task.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
In a verified-local seat VM, a worker or QA agent job runs with the pinned Node toolchain's bin first on its PATH. Both roles go through start_job.
- The PATH is toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH, the check job's form. toolchain=TOOLCHAIN ('/opt/moe/toolchain') is injectable from Python only.
- So a bare node, npm or npx resolves to /opt/moe/toolchain/bin, and npm's #!/usr/bin/env node shebang finds that node.

The supervisor's export (the candidate the host imports) skips a real directory named exactly node_modules when no manifest path lies under it.
- Such a directory is neither walked nor emitted. It adds no entry, delete, byte or visit past its own name.
- So an in-place npm ci neither poisons a worker's candidate (symlinks, entry and byte caps) nor refuses a QA job's empty candidate.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Prepend the toolchain bin to JOB_PATH itself: rejected. check_job already builds toolchain + '/bin:' + JOB_PATH, so its PATH would list the bin twice, and check_job must stay byte-unchanged.
- A Python-only toolchain keyword on start_job: chosen. It is check_job's own seam shape, it lets J5 inject a stub toolchain, and main() needs no change because it forwards **seams.
- Skip every node_modules: rejected. A repository that vendors node_modules would silently lose real edits and deletes. The manifest-based vendored set keeps tracked trees walked.
- Honor .gitignore or a list of build directories: out of scope by the task. It would put a parser inside the security boundary; only node_modules is skipped.
- Filter at emit time instead of skipping the walk: rejected. It still visits thousands of names against WALK_LIMIT. X8's WALK_LIMIT 8/7 row pins the skip-before-descend.
- Prove precedence over /usr/local/bin with a real node there: a non-root test cannot write /usr/local/bin. J5 puts a shadow dir at the head of m.JOB_PATH instead, and J3/J4 pin the real PATH string.
- Extend X2's table: X2 is EXPORT_BASE-only. Separate X8/X9 rows keep the tracked base local, and task-7d154d34's `^[JX][0-9]+ ` pattern still re-runs them.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- start_job reads the JOB_PATH global at call time, so a harness can patch m.JOB_PATH. The J rows never call check_job.
- Export counts self.visited while it lists a directory, before sorting and lstat, so a skipped name costs exactly one visit.
- finish() emits a delete for every manifest path that was never added to seen. Directories are never added, so the skip cannot hide a tracked deletion.
- J4's probe runs as the real job through GUARD (NoNewPrivs, and a PID namespace when root). So J5's stubs exercise the exec path a real agent uses, including /usr/bin/env's PATH lookup.
- On success, Node 24's spec reporter ends with the 8-line summary. On failure it prints a failing-tests section after that summary. Hence tail -n8 and tail -n60 in the gate.
- task-7d154d34 (WORKING, dependsOn this row) re-runs this row's J/X rows and certificationEvidence.test.ts in its own gate, and its governor runbook builds the plugin from this row's landing. architect-3669a6f6's comment on this row confirms the J<n>/X<n> naming and the J3/J4 literal.
